rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunk 0 lede 'The machine you just met can be steered' is the rule's OWN worked carve-out example verbatim ('the machine you just met' is quoted in rule 1's module-arc-beats-in-openers/closers carve-out). Chunk 6 line 47 'wrote what the session taught you into ./CLAUDE.local.md' and line 44 header 'You just ran the same loop' resolve against the module's just-completed exercise: getting-going.md lists '[Compound and close](exercises/compound-and-close.md)' immediately before this lecture's include-link, and compound-and-close.md's own body ('let Claude review the whole session and write your ./CLAUDE.local.md from session evidence. Push back where it misread.') matches the claim exactly — resolved via the module-arc-closer carve-out, not stranded. Chunk 7 line 61 'The file you wrote today' and 'the bug' carry forward the same session-artifact referent under the same carve-out. Chunk 7 line 63 'The loop is the shape' resolves against chunk 6's own header ('You just ran the same loop'), a term named on an earlier slide of the same file and reused — the rule's own NOT-violation example shape.

Chunk 1 line 10 'the opening lecture's mirror' is unpacked in the same sentence ('the LLM that flatters you, calls unfinished work progress, mirrors your stance') — the compendium's own worked PASS example. Chunk 6 line 47 'The way this training was built is the shape you just ran on your own repo' names the training's own construction (attested by the 'training-construction' backing source) rather than pointing at another document by position; the dissolved 'how-this-training-was-built' file this content was absorbed from no longer exists, so there is no sibling file being pointed at. No new cross-file callback in the added chunks.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: `grep -n "the-machine-you-just-met\|compound-and-close" curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/getting-going.md` confirms the module include order: '[Compound and close](exercises/compound-and-close.md)' (line 50) directly precedes '[The machine you just met](lectures/the-machine-you-just-met.md)' (line 52) with no other lecture between. Read compound-and-close.md directly: it is the exercise where Claude drafts './CLAUDE.local.md' from session evidence and the student pushes back where it misreads — the exact beat chunk 6-7 name. Not a dead reference.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: no guess-before-reveal demo shape anywhere; the only hit for /guess|predict/ (`grep -niE '\bguess\b|\bpredict'`) is line 8's unrelated 'predict the next likely word'

rules_evaluated.evidence: Every chunk, including the two new ones, carries a self-standing claim: chunk 6 (lines 47-49) states and attributes the compounding loop in three sentences; chunk 7 (lines 54-63) states Klaassen's definition, unpacks it in four bullets, and closes on a synthesis line. Neither is a bare wait-state or single context-dependent bullet.

Line 44 'You just ran the same loop' is directly supported by lines 47-49 describing the found-wrongness/corrected/wrote-it-down cycle. Line 51 'What compounds' is directly answered by the four bullets at lines 56-59. Neither header is contradicted by its own chunk.

Per sub-item, whole-body mechanical checks: 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction — `grep -nE 'Not [A-Za-z]+\. Not '` → 0 hits. Anaphora/epistrophe triples — `grep -nE '\. [A-Z][a-z]+ [a-z]+\. [A-Z][a-z]+ [a-z]+\. [A-Z][a-z]+ [a-z]+\.'` → 0 hits (Klaassen's four bullets at lines 56-59 are a quoted definitional list with four distinct subjects — features/bug fixes/patterns/codebase — not a repeated-clause triple). Self-grading superlatives — `grep -niE 'one of the (most|best)|most (useful|valuable|important)|the single (most|best)'` → 0 hits. Number + own retraction — the nine-in-ten/seven-step line (line 24) is pre-existing and carries the maintainer's own 'illustration, not a measurement' label, the compendium's named attested-exception shape; unchanged by this diff. Abstraction-noun stacks and empty-leg verb triplets — none in the new chunks (line 61's 'a pattern, codified... a test... a doc that stops lying' are concrete objects, not abstraction nouns).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No repo/maintainer vocabulary (compendium, surface-as-noun, beat, mood, forcing function) appears anywhere in the body. 'Compound engineering' (line 49) and 'the loop' (line 44/63) are ordinary engineering vocabulary explicitly attributed to an external practitioner (Kieran Klaassen) being taught to the room, not maintainer-internal dialect smuggled in as unexplained jargon; './CLAUDE.local.md' (line 47) is a real filename the student produced, not dialect.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: `grep -n '\*\*'` on the body projection returns exactly 3 hits total in the whole file: line 9 '**sycophancy**', line 24 '**error cascade**', line 49 '**compound engineering**' — one coined-term handle per naming slide, each ≤2 words. Chunk 7 ('What compounds', lines 51-63) carries 0 bold despite its 4-bullet list, consistent with the maintainer's accept-note that the quoted definition is a list, not a bolded-lead-per-bullet slide. Loop slides (6-7) stay prose/list, never a bolded-lead-per-bullet pattern.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Six of seven `##` headings are full declarative claims (e.g. line 20 'A check resets the chain', line 44 'You just ran the same loop'). Line 51 'What compounds' is the closest to violating: it is a noun-clause topic label rather than a subject-predicate claim. It sits inside the compendium's own catalogue-entry-naming-its-subject NOT-violation bucket (parallel to the rule's own examples 'The numbers' / 'Verification, named') — it introduces Klaassen's quoted external definition and four illustrative bullets, and the maintainer block (line 78) explicitly attests this as 'the definitional slide' whose job is to name the subject of a quoted definition, not to assert a claim of its own. Stays inside.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest candidate: line 63 closer 'The loop is the shape. The bug today was the excuse.' reads like it could restate header 44 ('You just ran the same loop'), the (c) aphorism-kicker shape. It stays inside because the second sentence adds a genuine reframe not present anywhere earlier — it inverts foreground/background (the day's bug was the vehicle, not the point) rather than re-announcing the loop; the maintainer block (Placement paragraph) explicitly names and defends this exact line as 'the designed hand-off into ## Next,' an existing accept-note on the passage. Line 61 ('The file you wrote today is the smallest unit that qualifies... A test that proves the bug is the same move in a different file. So is a doc that stops lying.') maps Klaassen's abstract definition onto three concrete instances (rules file, test, doc) — new content, not (a) doctrine restatement. Line 47 ('The way this training was built is the shape you just ran') is the beat's load-bearing payload (attested by the training-construction backing source), not (b) gratuitous self-referential design commentary about being inside a pedagogy.
